Open to everyone

Accessibility

I want this site to work for everyone who's looking for a home or a space on Vashon.

Here's what I'm aiming for, what the site checks, where it falls short, and how to tell me when something gets in your way. This statement is dated $statement_date.

What the site checks Tell me about a barrier

What I'm aiming for

I'm aiming for WCAG 2.1 at level AA, the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines from the W3C. It's a target I work toward, and I'd rather tell you where I fall short than claim I've got there.

What the site checks

The site's own automated tests open every kind of page in a real browser, at a desktop width and at a phone width, and check these things.

  • Structure

    Every page has one main heading and headings in order, plus the landmarks screen readers use to jump around: header, navigation, main and footer.

  • Names

    Every link, button, form field and image has a name a screen reader can read, and every form field has its label.

  • Keyboard

    The first stop when you press Tab is a "Skip to content" link, and every stop after it shows a visible focus ring.

  • Contrast

    Text meets the AA levels of contrast, 4.5 to 1, or 3 to 1 for large text, both at rest and when you hover over it.

  • Less motion

    If your device asks for less motion, smooth scrolling stops, the map stops animating, and counters show their final numbers at once.

  • Small screens

    Pages are checked at 390 pixels wide, a common phone width, and they don't scroll sideways.

Automated checks can't find everything. They don't replace people using screen readers, magnifiers, voice control or a keyboard alone, which is why I want to hear from you.

The map and the list

The map is one way in, never the only way. Every place on it is also a card in the list beside it, and the pins can be reached and opened with the keyboard.

With JavaScript turned off you can still read the listings: each place has its own plain page, and the Listings page shows a simple list of everything that's open.

Where it falls short

Some pages you may reach from here aren't mine to change: the Windermere Vashon site, the thank-you page Netlify shows after you send a form, and the Stripe pages where tenants and owners handle payments. Other companies run them.

Ledger, the portal for tenants and owners, and the lease documents on courthousesquarevashon.com are separate from this site too, and the checks above don't cover them.

Tell me what got in your way

If something here is hard to use, or you'd like a page in another format, I'd like to know.

Email me at me@ebberry.com. Tell me what you were trying to do and what got in the way. I'll fix what I can and write back.

A friend to Vashon.
